data.name: Gautom
data.gender_notes: Gautom is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Gautom is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Gov' meaning 'cow' and 'm' meaning 'protector'. This name is a reverence to Lord Krishna, who is often depicted as the protector of cows and the God of agriculture. In Hindu tradition, Lord Krishna is considered the embodiment of love, compassion, and wisdom. The name Gautom carries the meaning “God of agriculture” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gautom usually hope their child will grow to embody god of agriculture and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine protector and provider, representing love, compassion, and wisdom.
data.etymology: Gautom belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of agriculture.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gautom total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Gautam is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Gautama', which means 'he who has arrived' or 'he who is vast'. It is associated with the enlightened sage, Mahavira, and the revered Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, emphasizing spiritual growth and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Gautam is the name of the legendary sage who is the author of the ancient Hindu scripture known as Mahabharata, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India. Mahabharata is believed to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE. It is a massive poem of 100,000 shlokas (verses) and is considered one of the greatest works of Indian literature.

Gautam is also the birth name of Siddhartha Gautama, who is better known as the Buddha. He lived in the 5th century BCE and is the founder of Buddhism. Gautama renounced his princely life and embarked on a quest for enlightenment, which he achieved under the Bodhi tree.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern usage, the name 'Gautom' is often associated with the concepts of AI automation, DevOps, and cloud computing. For instance, a Microsoft Azure Developer might call an automated pipeline 'Gautom Pipeline'. Similarly, a DevOps engineer managing a Google Cloud Platform deployment could refer to an autoscaling group as 'Gautom Group'. The name 'Gautom' is a nod to the Hindu god 'Gautama' and the automation and trend-setting ideals associated with the deity.
